title: Cost export & print-friendly view: visual consistency, accessibility, and redlines
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Design a cohesive export and print-friendly experience for the Redwood Console cost views (cost breakdowns, tiles, and drilldowns) that preserves key visual hierarchy, supports accessibility requirements (WCAG AA), and reduces manual formatting work for customers wanting PDF/print artifacts. This ticket tracks the review cycle, stakeholder feedback, visual redlines, QA checklist, and engineering handoff artifacts for the initial implementation.

Scope: - Export formats: PDF (print-optimized) + CSV for tabular data. - Print stylesheet: condensed layout, hide interactive controls (filters, tooltips), ensure color-contrast-safe palettes for charts, and include metadata header (date range, environment, model/version). - Desktop-first prototype with responsive fallback for narrow-width exports triggered from console "Export" menu. - Accessibility: ensure semantic headings, table summaries, descriptive alt text for small sparklines, and keyboard-focusable export flow.

Design goals and constraints: - Preserve cost attribution ordering and highlight anomalies while fitting onto 1-2 A4 pages for summary exports. - Avoid pixel-perfect parity with console UI where it hurts readability on paper (e.g., skip micro-animations and dense tooltips). - Work within the current console theming tokens and brand-approved print palette. - Minimize backend changes: prefer client-side generation of print-optimized HTML/PDF where possible; engineering has flagged server-side CSV export as lower-risk for MVP.
comments: 2025-11-18 - Asha Patel: Initial design spike complete. Uploaded Figma frames covering 1-page summary PDF, expanded 2-page breakdown, and table CSV spec. Noted two unknowns: header metadata cadence (who owns ‘environment’ string) and chart export exact rendering for stacked vs grouped bars.

2025-11-19 - Marco Ruiz (PM): Reviewed. Prioritize PDF summary + CSV for launch. Add model/version to header and include customer-facing labeling differences for Dedicated vs Hosted customers. Suggest adding a small 'Export context' callout when export initiated (captures applied filters).

2025-11-20 - Tom Gallagher (Eng): Engineering review: client-side html-to-pdf approach acceptable for MVP; suggest avoid canvas rasterization for charts — prefer SVG export to preserve accessibility. Backend CSV endpoint is fine but needs pagination support. Flagged print CSS edgecases around flex-wrapping in cost tiles.

2025-11-21 - Accessibility review (Nina Lopez): Request: ensure table markup includes <caption> and scope attributes, provide longdesc (or linked description) for complex charts, and confirm sufficient color contrast for chart palettes when printed in grayscale. Recommended updated palette tokens and ARIA descriptions in Figma annotations.

2025-11-22 - Design review session notes (Evelyn Chen): Stakeholders (Product, Eng, Security, Success) walked through prototype. Feedback: - Move metadata header to top-right, reduce font-weight, and align to brand legal copy style. - Add visual indicator for 'sampled metrics' when sampling is applied. - QA to validate breakpoints when varying row counts cause page overflow. Actions assigned and captured below.

2025-11-24 - Asha Patel: Applied final redlines: swapped to high-contrast token pair for bar fills, added table caption and descriptive summary block for each exported chart, collapsed secondary CTA for 'Download CSV' into kebab menu to simplify print view. Uploaded revised Figma and updated spec doc. Ready for engineering handoff.

2025-11-25 - Engineering handoff (Tom Gallagher): Handoff accepted pending two follow-ups: (1) provide JS util for SVG->PDF conversion and (2) small polyfill for table-break-inside CSS in Safari print. Eng assigned ENG-7832 for CSV pagination and ENG-7833 for client-side PDF toolchain.
